title: When the Archive Breaks
premise: Paloma Thornbury, a xenolinguist who lost her ability to dream in human languages after a classified incident aboard the research station Meridian, has spent fifteen years hauling cargo through contested orbits, hiding in plain sight. When gravity flickers system-wide for exactly nine seconds, she realizes the anomaly is a signal — one encoded in the alien language only she can still read. Hunted by both warring governments and the ghost of her old mentor who caused the original catastrophe, Paloma must carry the message to the neutral relay at Kestrel's Reach before the fleets converge. In the end she chooses truth over loyalty to everyone who protected her silence, broadcasting the message and exposing the war's manufactured origin — ending the war, but erasing the last of her old identity forever.
about_author: Lior Okonkwo is a former maritime radio operator turned science fiction writer whose work explores language, exile, and the ethics of witness. They live between coastal cities and write on ships whenever possible.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Mid-haul through contested orbit, gravity fails for exactly nine seconds; cargo drifts, crew panics, and Paloma alone notices the flicker pulsed in a pattern she recognizes from dreams she no longer has. Beat: dread reawakening.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Cargo
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. She inspects her hold and finds a sealed canister that isn't on any manifest, addressed in Meridian station notation. Her first mate, Dov, urges her to jettison it. Beat: the past knocking.

chapters.title: Dreams Without Words
chapters.summary: POV Paloma, flashback-woven. We learn how she stopped dreaming in human languages after Meridian, and how both governments classified her file. Beat: grief for the self she buried.

chapters.title: The Man Who Should Be Dead
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Her old mentor, Dr. Ilsa Vane — officially dead fifteen years — hails her ship, claiming the nine-second flicker was her doing and that Paloma must deliver what's in the canister to Kestrel's Reach. Beat: distrust tangled with longing.

chapters.title: Manifests and Lies
chapters.summary: POV Dov. The first mate secretly reports the anomaly to his faction handlers, torn between loyalty to Paloma and his own people trapped behind enemy lines. Beat: betrayal seeded by love.

chapters.title: Interdiction at Ceres Gate
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. A warship demands inspection; Paloma hides the canister inside a dying crewmate's medical pod, crossing a line she can't uncross. Beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: What the Canister Says
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Alone, she decodes fragments: the message proves the war began with a deliberate translation error at Meridian — an error authored by someone still powerful. Beat: vertigo of truth.

chapters.title: The Neutral Ground
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. She docks at a smuggler haven to resupply and finds wanted posters bearing her face, issued by both sides simultaneously. Beat: invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vane. Flashback chapter: Vane reveals she falsified the original translation to prevent a worse discovery, and chose Paloma as courier because only a 'broken' linguist can verify it. Beat: mentor as architect.

chapters.title: Dov's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Dov. His handlers order him to seize the canister or his family loses protection. He sabotages the ship's nav instead, buying time without betraying her outright. Beat: loyalty bending.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Debris Fields
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Both fleets' black-ops ships pursue her through a graveyard of war wreckage; she survives by reading debris patterns like grammar. Beat: skill as survival, cost mounting.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Prison
chapters.summary: POV Paloma, captured briefly. An intelligence officer offers her amnesty and a return to linguistic work if she surrenders the canister unopened. Beat: temptation of the old life.

chapters.title: Escape Is Not Freedom
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Freed by Dov's mutiny, she realizes every faction now knows the route to Kestrel's Reach; delivering the message may trigger the very war it should end. Beat: despair before resolve.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds Again
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. Gravity flickers a second time — longer, wrong — and stations begin failing. The signal is degrading; the window to deliver it is closing. Beat: ticking clock made physical.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Sacrifice
chapters.summary: POV Dov. He confesses everything to Paloma and offers himself as decoy. She refuses to let him die for her silence's sins. Beat: forgiveness under pressure.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Reach
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Arrival at the neutral relay, where representatives of both fleets wait armed, and Vane appears alive before everyone. Beat: convergence.

chapters.title: The Trial Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. With no court willing to hear the truth, Paloma improvises a public decoding — translating the message aloud before both fleets, making herself the evidence. Beat: courage as testimony.

chapters.title: What the Message Actually Says
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. The full broadcast: not surrender terms, but the aliens' own record proving the war's origin — and an offer of contact contingent on peace. Fleets hesitate. Beat: revelation.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Translation
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Vane. Confronted, Vane takes responsibility publicly and dies destroying the last copy of her falsified archive. Beat: justice outside the law, paid in full.

chapters.title: Ceasefire in Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. Weapons stand down across the system as the flicker returns one final time — gentle now, an acknowledgment. Beat: awe and release.

chapters.title: A Language of Her Own
chapters.summary: POV Paloma. Offered reinstatement and honors, Paloma declines, choosing to help build the new contact protocols on her own terms. Beat: identity remade.

chapters.title: First Dream
chapters.summary: POV Paloma, epilogue. Months later, hauling peaceful cargo, Paloma dreams for the first time in fifteen years — in a language that is neither human nor alien, but hers. Beat: quiet hope.
